items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: At the time you joined Duke, the 12 members of the band were Johnny Hodges, Barney Bigard, Harry Carney, Arthur Whetsel, Cootie Williams, Freddie Jenkins, Joe Nanton, Fred Guy, Wellman Braud, Sonny Greer, and Duke, is that right? Right. Uh-huh.

ctx.x: There was never anything written down?

Yes. There were sort of skeleton arrangements. The solos weren't written. It was like, say the next 32 bars of Cootie, or Brown, or Johnny Hodges, or like that. That's the way it was on the arrangements. No one wrote any solos for anybody.
You never did with Ellington, did you?

items.title: 56712_Cootie Williams oral history interview
items.q: Lawrence? No, I think it was Tizol, wasn't it? I can't recall which one came first.

ctx.x: Well, it seems to me that one of the first people he put on was Lawrence.
Lawrence? No, I think it was Tizol, wasn't it? I can't recall which one came first.
